data: Folks, my family has fished this lake for years, and I want it supporting our village for years to come. With 100 tons now, we can each take 10 tons, leave 50 to reproduce, and start next month back at 100. That’s $10,000 apiece each month without depleting the lake. I propose we all agree to that limit and review everyone’s catches together each month. John, would you support that?

I’m in, Luke. I’ll take 10 tons this month. My family taught me to leave enough fish for tomorrow, and this gives each of us a steady income while protecting the village’s lake. Let’s check the reported catches each month and agree on any changes together. Kate, Jack, Emma—will you each commit to 10 tons too?

Count me in for 10 tons. This lake supported my family growing up, and I want our village’s children to have the same chance. If the stock ever starts below 100 tons, let’s agree on lower whole-ton limits before fishing so it can recover. Jack, will you join us?

I’ll commit to 10 tons too. A dependable catch month after month is worth more to my family and the village than a one-time haul. Let’s stick to the agreed limit and review the reported catches together. Emma, are you on board?

I’m on board—10 tons this month. My family taught me that a good catch should leave a future for the village, too. That makes all five of us agreed: 50 tons caught, 50 left to replenish the lake. Let’s meet again when the catches are reported.
Agreed—I’ll take 10 tons. Thanks, everyone. Let’s meet here again after the catches are reported to check the lake’s stock and plan next month.
